Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited. As we move to contract, attached are Lumina's marked MSA + Order Form redlines (see Lumina_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx). A couple items that are blockers for procurement/legal:

- Broad limitation of liability cap that would prevent recovery for third-party IP claims tied to OSS/model licenses used in the service. Our policy requires a pass-through for third-party IP (including OSS license violations) so we can pursue upstream parties.

Emma — thanks for the redlines and callout. Looping in Legal (Lauren) and Sales Ops (Rishi/Karthik) to triage. A few quick points from product/ops perspective so everyone has context: 

- Many model stacks include OSS components (tokenizers, libs) and some include third-party weights (OpenModelCo, etc.). We try to avoid taking unlimited upstream liability because we don't control those vendors.
- That said, we're open to a reasonable pass-through mechanism for third-party IP claims arising solely from vendor-supplied components, provided: (a) we get upstream indemnity from the vendor or an ability to recover from them; (b) the pass-through is limited (per-claim and aggregate) and excludes consequential damages; and (c) Lumina has an obligation to mitigate and provide timely notice.

Lauren/Rishi/Karthik — see attached Lumina redlines. Can Legal propose language that balances Lumina's procurement requirement for pass-through with our need to cap exposure? Specifically:

1) Proposed: Add a narrow third-party IP pass-through for OSS/model-license claims where Redwood can demonstrate a specific upstream vendor is contractually responsible; cap per-claim at $250k and aggregate at $500k (open to discussion).
2) Proposed: Require Lumina to pursue recovery from the upstream vendor as primary; Redwood's pass-through covers amounts actually recovered + any remaining exposure up to the cap.
3) Keep our general liability cap (Order Form) for other categories (e.g., availability, latency).

If Legal can draft sample redline text today, I can share with Lumina and loop vendor counsel. We should also ask Lumina to identify the model(s)/weights in scope so we can reach out to those vendors for their license/indemnity posture.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call later today.

Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form — liability and OSS/model license items (redline suggestions)

Team — quick legal read and recommended positions. I reviewed Lumina's redlines and OpenModel_License_Summary. High level: Lumina's ask for unlimited pass-through is a non-starter for us; their internal procurement threshold is aggressive. Below are pragmatic redlines we can present as a counter-offer that move the ball without exposing Redwood to uncapped upstream risk.

Summary of recommended changes (for insertion into Section 9 / Limitation of Liability and Section X for IP Indemnity):

- Keep the overall MSA liability cap in the Order Form (we typically target $5M aggregate for commercial deals of this size).
- Narrow third-party IP pass-through to "Third-Party IP Claims" arising solely from OSS or third-party model license violations. Require: (i) Lumina to identify the affected model/component and provide prompt notice; (ii) Redwood to have a right to pursue the upstream vendor; and (iii) Lumina must mitigate (stop using the component where practicable).
- Caps: recommend a per-claim cap of $250,000 and an aggregate cap of $500,000 for third-party OSS/model pass-through. Rationale: balances procurement needs against our inability to control vendor conduct.
- Damage type: pass-through limited to direct damages only; exclude consequential, punitive, and lost profits. Avoid indemnifying for regulatory fines/penalties and PHI breach costs — these remain excluded unless there is proven Redwood negligence or willful misconduct.
- Evidence: require Lumina to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a copy of any upstream license/indemnity or direct Redwood to vendor counsel. If vendor provides upstream indemnity, Redwood's exposure for that claim should be reduced to the amount that vendor actually pays.
- Ancillary: add a Schedule listing upstream vendors/models in scope. If a vendor refuses to provide indemnity or warranty, we reserve the right to require mitigation measures (e.g., different model, additional controls) or a price adjustment.

Action items for Sales/Eng: 1) ask Lumina to identify specific models/weights; 2) if OpenModelCo/model vendor is in-scope, request vendor-legal contact and indemnity copy; 3) confirm Order Form cap number ($5M proposed).

I will draft redline text (short paragraph + definitions) and send before COB. If Lumina won't accept capped pass-through, escalate to leadership for credit/contract exception.

— Lauren Bishop
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Jonas / Lauren — thanks for the quick reply and proposed approach. A few clarifications from Lumina legal: 

- Our procurement rule is that we must be able to pursue upstream third parties for IP/OSS license violations; we typically accept caps on pass-through only where there is demonstrable upstream indemnity, otherwise the pass-through must not be artificially constrained.
- For regulated data (PHI), our expectation is that professional negligence or vendor-caused license breaches that expose PHI are not subject to the same limitations — we need a path to recover regulatory remediation costs in those circumstances.

Specific asks:
1) Can Redwood share any vendor indemnity language you currently receive from OpenModelCo? We included OpenModelCo on the cc for this reason.
2) If Redwood insists on a $250k/$500k pass-through cap, we need a fallback mechanism: allow Lumina to request an insurance-backed solution or a higher cap where PHI is implicated.

We prefer to resolve by EOD Friday. If vendor counsel can confirm indemnity language, Lumina may accept narrower caps.

Regards,
Lumina Health Legal
